Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. ![Continuous Integration](https://github.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/workflows/Continuous%20Integration/badge.svg)

# BackWPup - WordPress Backup Plugin
Schedule complete automatic backups of your WordPress installation. Decide which content will be stored (Dropbox, S3…). This is the free version

## Description
The **backup plugin** **[BackWPup Pro](http://backwpup.com/)** can be used to save your complete installation including /wp-content/ and push them to an external Backup Service, like **Dropbox**, **S3**, **FTP** and many more, see list below. With a single backup .zip file you are able to easily restore an installation.

BackWPup Free is the number 1 backup-plugin for WordPress with nearly 1.000.000 downloads and in the top 20 of all WordPress Plugins (checked on rankwp.com)

* Database Backup  *(needs mysqli)*
* WordPress XML Export
* Generate a file with installed plugins
* Optimize Database
* Check and repair Database
* File backup
* Backups in zip, tar, tar.gz format *(needs gz, ZipArchive)*
* Store backup to directory
* Store backup to FTP server *(needs ftp)*
* Store backup to Dropbox *(needs curl)*
* Store backup to S3 services *(needs curl)*
* Store backup to Microsoft Azure (Blob) *(needs curl)*
* Store backup to RackSpaceCloud *(needs PHP curl)*
* Store backup to SugarSync *(needs curl)*
* Store backup to Amazon Glacier *(needs PHP curl)*
* Store backup to Google Drive *(needs curl)*
* Store backup to OneDrive *(needs curl)*
* Store backup to HiDrive *(needs curl)*
* Send logs and backups by email
* Multi-site support only as network admin

**Remember: The most expensive backup is the one you never did! And please test your backups!**

**Made by [WP Media](https://wp-media.me) · We love WordPress**

## Requirements
* PHP >= 7.4
* WordPress >=4.9
* To use the Plugin with full functionality PHP 7.4 with mysqli, FTP,gz, ZipArchive and curl is needed.
* Plugin functions that don't work because of your server settings, will not be displayed in admin area.

## Screenshots

1. [Working job and jobs overview](https://raw.github.com/inpsyde/backwpup/master/screenshot-1.png)
2. [Job creation/edit](https://raw.github.com/inpsyde/backwpup/master/screenshot-2.png)
3. [Displaying logs](https://raw.github.com/inpsyde/backwpup/master/screenshot-3.png)
4. [Manage backup archives](https://raw.github.com/inpsyde/backwpup/master/screenshot-4.png)
5. [Dashboard](https://raw.github.com/inpsyde/backwpup/master/screenshot-5.png)

## Development

### Install dependencies & build

- `$ composer install`
- `$ npm install`
- `$ sudo npm install --global gulp-cli`
- `$ gulp buildAssets`

### Unit tests and code style

1. `$ composer install`
2. `$ ./vendor/bin/phpunit`

### Building a release package

If you want to build a release package
(that can be used for deploying a new version on wordpress.org or manual installation on a WP website via ZIP uploading),
follow these steps:

1. Run the commands from "Install dependencies & build"
2. The following command should get you a Free version ZIP file ready to be used on a WordPress site:

```
$ gulp free --packageVersion=?.?.? --compressPath=.
```
or for crate the PRO Version Zip for the german shop:

```
$ gulp pro --packageVersion=?.?.? --compressPath=. --language=de
```

content.thinking:
Now I have a good picture of the plugin. Let me think about what major new feature would be most valuable from a business perspective.

BackWPup is a WordPress backup plugin. Key existing features:
- Database backup
- File backup
- Multiple storage providers (S3, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, FTP, Azure, etc.)
- Scheduled backups
- Backup restore
- MCP integration (a current feature being developed - feature/mcp branch)
- Pro version with additional features

From a business perspective, what major features could be valuable?

1. **Smart/Incremental Backup with AI-powered anomaly detection** - Only backup changed files since last backup (incremental), which saves storage and time. Many competitors already have this.


2. **One-click restore with staging** - Restore to a staging environment first before production. Very valuable for agencies and businesses.
3. **Backup Verification / Integrity Testing** - Automatically test backups by restoring them to a temporary environment and verifying they work. This is a huge pain point - "the backup that exists but doesn't work."
4. **Multi-site Dashboard / Agency features** - Manage backups across multiple WordPress sites from one central dashboard. Very valuable for agencies/freelancers managing dozens of client sites.
5. **White-labeling** - Let agencies white-label the plugin for clients.
6. **Real-time/Continuous backup** - Backup as changes happen, similar to how version control systems work.
7. **Disaster Recovery as a Service** - Managed recovery service where BackWPup team helps you restore.
8. **Security Integration** - Detect malware and compromised files in backups, then isolate them.
9. **WooCommerce-specific backup** - Intelligently backup orders, products, and customer data with minimal downtime.
10. **Backup from Backup** - Move backups between different cloud storage providers.

Given their existing MCP integration work and Pro version business model, the multi-site agency dashboard stands out as the strongest differentiator in a crowded market with competitors like UpdraftPlus and Jetpack Backup.

A centralized dashboard for managing hundreds of WordPress sites could become its own SaaS product or premium tier, directly addressing UpdraftPlus's weakness and commanding a higher price point for agencies. Alternatively, automated backup verification—testing restores in temporary environments to confirm backups actually work—solves the critical problem users face of not knowing if their backup is functional until disaster strikes. Real-time continuous backup for WooCommerce sites that can't tolerate losing hours of transaction data is also high-value for ecommerce. The multi-site agency dashboard seems most compelling because it creates recurring SaaS revenue, targets high-LTV agency customers, and fills a clear market gap.

Voici mon analyse après avoir parcouru la structure du projet :

---

## Feature la plus impactante business : **Agency Dashboard — gestion multi-sites centralisée**

### Pourquoi c'est le meilleur choix

**Le problème** : Les agences et freelances gèrent des dizaines/centaines de sites WordPress. Aujourd'hui, ils doivent se connecter sur chaque site séparément pour vérifier l'état des backups.

**Ce que ça apporterait** :
- Un dashboard centralisé (SaaS ou plugin réseau) pour voir tous les backups de tous les clients en un coup d'oeil
- Alertes centralisées (un backup a échoué chez le client X)
- Déclenchement de backups à distance, download/restore depuis une interface unique

**Pourquoi c'est fort business** :
- **LTV élevée** : les agences ont 20-200 sites, elles paient plus et churnent moins que les particuliers
- **Upsell naturel** : justifie un tier de prix "Agency" 3-5x supérieur au Pro standard
- **Lock-in fort** : une fois qu'une agence gère 50 sites via ton dashboard, elle ne part plus
- **UpdraftPlus, le concurrent n°1, est mauvais là-dessus** — c'est une fenêtre d'opportunité

---

## Feature #2 forte : **Vérification automatique d'intégrité des backups**

Le message marketing est imbattable : *"Le seul backup plugin qui vérifie automatiquement que ton backup fonctionne vraiment."*

Concrètement : après chaque backup, restauration dans un environnement temporaire éphémère + screenshot + rapport. C'est le pain point #1 des utilisateurs (un backup corrompu qu'on découvre au moment de la catastrophe).

---

**Je recommanderais le dashboard agency** — c'est le meilleur ratio différenciation / revenus potentiels, et ça s'articule bien avec le fait que vous avez déjà une API REST et l'intégration MCP en cours sur ce repo.

Tu veux qu'on explore l'une des deux plus en profondeur ?
D'ailleurs faudrait avoir des features Pro et Free parce que y a une version gratuite du plugin aussi

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace WPMedia\BackWPup\Backup;

use WPMedia\BackWPup\Backup\FailureContext\FailureDisplayDetailsProviderInterface;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Backup\FailureContext\FailureDisplayDetailsResolver;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Backup\FailureContext\GenericFailureDisplayDetailsProvider;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Backup\FailureContext\GDrive\GDriveFailureDisplayDetailsProvider;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Backup\FailureContext\Glacier\GlacierFailureDisplayDetailsProvider;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Backup\FailureContext\HiDrive\HiDriveFailureDisplayDetailsProvider;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Backup\FailureContext\OneDrive\OneDriveFailureDisplayDetailsProvider;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Dependencies\League\Container\ServiceProvider\AbstractServiceProvider;

class ServiceProviderPro extends AbstractServiceProvider {

	/**
	 * Service provided by this provider.
	 *
	 * @var array
	 */
	protected $provides = [
		'failure_display_details_resolver',
	];

	/**
	 * Subscribers provided by this provider.
	 *
	 * @var array
	 */
	public $subscribers = [];

	/**
	 * Check if the service provider provides a specific service.
	 *
	 * @param string $id The id of the service.
	 * @return bool
	 */
	public function provides( string $id ): bool {
		return in_array( $id, $this->provides, true );
	}

	/**
	 * Registers items with the container.
	 *
	 * @return void
	 */
	public function register(): void {
		$this->getContainer()->addShared( 'onedrive_failure_display_details_provider', OneDriveFailureDisplayDetailsProvider::class );
		$this->getContainer()->addShared( 'gdrive_failure_display_details_provider', GDriveFailureDisplayDetailsProvider::class );
		$this->getContainer()->addShared( 'hidrive_failure_display_details_provider', HiDriveFailureDisplayDetailsProvider::class );
		$this->getContainer()->addShared( 'glacier_failure_display_details_provider', GlacierFailureDisplayDetailsProvider::class );

		$this->getContainer()->extend( 'failure_display_details_resolver' )
			->setConcrete(
				/**
				 * Rebuild the resolver to keep the generic fallback as the final provider.
				 *
				 * @param FailureDisplayDetailsProviderInterface ...$providers Display details providers.
				 * @return FailureDisplayDetailsResolver
				 */
				static function ( FailureDisplayDetailsProviderInterface ...$providers ): FailureDisplayDetailsResolver {
					$generic_provider = null;
					$ordered          = [];

					foreach ( $providers as $provider ) {
						if ( $provider instanceof GenericFailureDisplayDetailsProvider ) {
							$generic_provider = $provider;
							continue;
						}

						$ordered[] = $provider;
					}

					if ( $generic_provider ) {
						$ordered[] = $generic_provider;
					}

					return new FailureDisplayDetailsResolver( ...$ordered );
				}
			)
			->addArgument( 'onedrive_failure_display_details_provider' )
			->addArgument( 'gdrive_failure_display_details_provider' )
			->addArgument( 'hidrive_failure_display_details_provider' )
			->addArgument( 'glacier_failure_display_details_provider' );
	}

	/**
	 * Returns the subscribers array.
	 *
	 * @return array
	 */
	public function get_subscribers() {
		return $this->subscribers;
	}
}
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli;

use BackWPup_File;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\BackupDecrypt;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\BackupEncrypt;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\JobExport;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\JobImport;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\Restore;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Dependencies\League\Container\ServiceProvider\AbstractServiceProvider;

/**
 * Service provider for Storage providers
 */
class ServiceProviderPro extends AbstractServiceProvider {
	/**
	 * Service provided by this provider
	 *
	 * @var array
	 */
	protected $provides = [
		SubscriberPro::class,
	];

	/**
	 * Subscribers provided by this provider
	 *
	 * @var array
	 */
	public $subscribers = [
		SubscriberPro::class,
	];

	/**
	 * Check if the service provider provides a specific service.
	 *
	 * @param string $id The id of the service.
	 *
	 * @return bool
	 */
	public function provides( string $id ): bool {
		return in_array( $id, $this->provides, true );
	}

	/**
	 * Registers items with the container
	 *
	 * @return void
	 */
	public function register(): void {

		if ( ! defined( 'WP_CLI' ) || ! WP_CLI ) {
			return;
		}

		$this->getContainer()->add( JobExport::class )
			->addArgument( $this->getContainer()->get( 'job_adapter' ) );
		$this->getContainer()->add( JobImport::class )
			->addArguments(
				[
					$this->getContainer()->get( 'job_adapter' ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( 'option_adapter' ),
				]
			);
		$this->getContainer()->add( BackupEncrypt::class );
		$this->getContainer()->add( BackupDecrypt::class );

		$this->getContainer()->add( BackWPup_File::class );
		$this->getContainer()->add( Restore::class )
			->addArguments(
				[
					$this->getContainer()->get( BackWPup_File::class ),
				]
			);

		$this->getContainer()->add( SubscriberPro::class )
			->addArgument(
				[
					$this->getContainer()->get( JobExport::class ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( JobImport::class ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( BackupEncrypt::class ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( BackupDecrypt::class ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( Restore::class ),
				]
			);
	}

	/**
	 * Returns the subscribers array
	 *
	 * @return array
	 */
	public function get_subscribers() {
		if ( ! defined( 'WP_CLI' ) || ! WP_CLI ) {
			return [];
		}
		return $this->subscribers;
	}
}

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli;

use BackWPup_File;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\BackupDecrypt;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\BackupEncrypt;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\JobExport;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\JobImport;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Cli\Commands\Restore;
use WPMedia\BackWPup\Dependencies\League\Container\ServiceProvider\AbstractServiceProvider;

/**
 * Service provider for Storage providers
 */
class ServiceProviderPro extends AbstractServiceProvider {
	/**
	 * Service provided by this provider
	 *
	 * @var array
	 */
	protected $provides = [
		SubscriberPro::class,
	];

	/**
	 * Subscribers provided by this provider
	 *
	 * @var array
	 */
	public $subscribers = [
		SubscriberPro::class,
	];

	/**
	 * Check if the service provider provides a specific service.
	 *
	 * @param string $id The id of the service.
	 *
	 * @return bool
	 */
	public function provides( string $id ): bool {
		return in_array( $id, $this->provides, true );
	}

	/**
	 * Registers items with the container
	 *
	 * @return void
	 */
	public function register(): void {

		if ( ! defined( 'WP_CLI' ) || ! WP_CLI ) {
			return;
		}

		$this->getContainer()->add( JobExport::class )
			->addArgument( $this->getContainer()->get( 'job_adapter' ) );
		$this->getContainer()->add( JobImport::class )
			->addArguments(
				[
					$this->getContainer()->get( 'job_adapter' ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( 'option_adapter' ),
				]
			);
		$this->getContainer()->add( BackupEncrypt::class );
		$this->getContainer()->add( BackupDecrypt::class );

		$this->getContainer()->add( BackWPup_File::class );
		$this->getContainer()->add( Restore::class )
			->addArguments(
				[
					$this->getContainer()->get( BackWPup_File::class ),
				]
			);

		$this->getContainer()->add( SubscriberPro::class )
			->addArgument(
				[
					$this->getContainer()->get( JobExport::class ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( JobImport::class ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( BackupEncrypt::class ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( BackupDecrypt::class ),
					$this->getContainer()->get( Restore::class ),
				]
			);
	}

	/**
	 * Returns the subscribers array
	 *
	 * @return array
	 */
	public function get_subscribers() {
		if ( ! defined( 'WP_CLI' ) || ! WP_CLI ) {
			return [];
		}
		return $this->subscribers;
	}
}
